title: Habib Rules Buckaroo Bowl I: The First Champion Is Crowned, and the Commish Gets the Basement Key
dek: Kaushal's Habibsters rode a 10-4 season and a 59-point Bowl blowout to the league's first title, while Sonny discovered that building the league does not mean winning it.
body: Every dynasty needs a first chapter, and the Buckaroo Football League's opened in 2023 with six managers, zero trust, and a trophy nobody had touched yet. By the end of it, Kaushal's name was the first one on it. Habibsters went 10-4, grabbed the No. 1 seed with 1,528.8 points, and then spent the playoffs making everyone else look like they were standing still. Habib was running away from the field all year, and this time nobody was writing him a ticket for it.

The regular season was a two-horse race at the top. Alan's Team Pillbert went 9-5 and posted the single biggest week of the year, a 156.18-point haymaker in week 3 that announced Philliberto was here to be a problem. Randy's The fumblers held the middle at a perfectly balanced 7-7, good for the 3 seed. And speaking of Randy, the league finished its inaugural season with exactly zero trades, a number that will surprise absolutely no one who has ever sent him an offer.

The hard-luck story of the year belongs to Mekhi. Dawgs scored 1,542.8 points, the most in the entire league, and somehow finished 6-8. Kai built the best scoring machine in the BFL and kept running into opponents having their week of the year at exactly the wrong time. He still snuck into the playoffs as the 4 seed, which is a little like getting a participation trophy for being the fastest car in the race.

The semifinals were two-week totals, and the top seeds held serve. Habibsters handled Dawgs 237.54 to 196.12, ending Mekhi's run of statistical injustice. On the other side, Team Pillbert outlasted The fumblers 234.86 to 216.44, sending Randy to the third-place finish and setting up the matchup the standings had been promising all season: No. 1 versus No. 2 in Buckaroo Bowl I.

It was not close. Kaushal dropped 251.36 points over the two weeks to Alan's 192.08, a 59-point beatdown that turned the first Buckaroo Bowl into a coronation. Fans of the league's resident villain had to watch the bad guy reach the final scene and get thrown off the cliff. Habibsters are the first champions in league history, and Habibi gets to tell everyone about it for 12 straight months.

Then there was the basement. Ramon's Araleasers went 4-10 and owned the season's lowest score, a 65.9 in week 9 that probably set off at least one controller. But the consolation ladder had other plans: Sonny's Ben Dover, despite a better 6-8 record and the 5 seed, lost its way down the ladder and finished dead last, with Brucie climbing to fifth. Yes, the commissioner who built the league finished at the bottom of it. Somewhere, a rules committee is already being formed.

So the record book now reads: Buckaroo Bowl I, Habibsters, champion; Ben Dover, last place. Kaushal set the bar, Alan got close enough to be mad about it, Mekhi has the points to prove he deserved better, and Sonny has a whole offseason to stare at the standings on the website he made. Year one is in the books. The grudges are just getting started.
